1 Utrum magi ex Oriente astrologi fuerint an non et cuiusnam generis fuerit
stella quae eos duxisse fertur, inde a priscis temporibus inter doctores christianos
quaestio controversa et plena dissensionis fuit, nec quicquam novi attulisse videtur
Manuel Comnenus; cf. quae congessit Bouché-Leclercq, Astrol. grecque, p. 610 ss.
sections.en:
1 Whether the magi from the East were astrologers or not and of what kind was
the star which is said to have led them, from ancient times among Christian teachers
has been a controversial question and full of disagreement, nor does Manuel Comnenus seem to have brought anything new;
cf. what Bouché-Leclercq has collected, Astrol. grecque, p. 610 ff.

summary.headline: The Magi and the Astrological Star
summary.text: Theological defense of astrology argues that human fallibility and divine miracles do not invalidate the art, citing Moses and the Gospel account of the Magi who followed a star. The Magi are presented as expert observers who inferred Christ’s place, nation, and nature from the star’s rising, zodiacal sign, inclination, and figure.
